news.title: World Cup final tug-of-war escalates as Morocco PM rebukes FA head, Spain stakes claim
news.lede: RABAT: The battle over who will host the 2030 World Cup final intensified on Friday after Morocco’s prime minister told his country’s football federation head to stop making promises before the Spanish FA chief insisted it should be held in Spain. Moroccan Prime Minister Aziz Akhannouch took aim at Royal Moroccan Football Federation (RMFF) President Fouzi Lekjaa, who boldly declared at a political party event that Casablanca would have the ‘honor’ of hosting the final. news.title: Wesley Sneijder puts World Cup prize and Cristiano Ronaldo treasure on sale for thousands
news.lede: The Dutch football legend retired from football in 2019, having starred for the likes of Real Madrid, Inter Milan and the Netherlands national team. Sneijder enjoyed a trophy-laden career, tasting league glory in Holland, Spain and Italy among his 20 major honours. He was at the peak of his powers in 2010, as he inspired Inter to treble success - including the Champions League - and scored five goals at the World Cup final to fire the Netherlands to the final. The playmaker continued to star on the European and international stage thereafter, turning out for Galatasaray and Nice before retiring at Qatari side Al Gharafa, and also played at the 2014 World Cup.

news.title: Pochettino’s ‘different’ vow to the US invites unwelcome speculation
news.lede: The US manager’s relationship with the international job has changed with a full World Cup cycle beginning. I hope, in this lifetime, you find someone who loves you the way Mauricio Pochettino loves Tottenham Hotspur. The grip Spurs have on his heart seems the stuff of a literary classic: his imperfect partner who called things off at the first sign of trouble must merely check in on him occasionally to rekindle hopes of a reunion. Perhaps a bit extreme, but this week’s revelation – that he’d return to Tottenham even if they were relegated and chalking his absence up to imperfect timing, not the part about handing the club a decade-old title – has implicity laid out the terms of his return as United States manager.

news.title: Canada routs Tanzania 6-0, waits to learn if it advances at U-20 Women's World Cup
news.lede: KATOWICE - Canada kept its FIFA Women's Under-20 World Cup hopes alive Friday with a 6-0 win over Tanzania in its final Group B match. Annabelle Chukwu scored twice, while Olivia Chisholm, Kaylee Hunter and Liana Tarasco also found the net. Tanzania's Ester Maseke opened the scoring with an own goal in the seventh minute. Canada finished third in Group B at 1-1-1 with four points.

news.title: Lekjaa’s World Cup 2030 Final Claim Riles FIFA, Spain
news.lede: Rabat – The debate over the venue for the 2030 World Cup final has intensified after Moroccan football chief Fouzi Lekjaa said the Hassan II Stadium would host the match, prompting FIFA and Spanish football officials to reiterate that no decision has been made. Fouzi Lekjaa, President of the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF) and a member of the Authenticity and Modernity Party (PAM) Political Bureau, made the claim during an electoral gathering in Benslimane Province on Thursday. “The province of Benslimane will have the honor of hosting the 2030 World Cup final,” he said, referring to the Hassan II Stadium currently under construction in the province. FIFA says no Lekjaa’s statement prompted a clarification from FIFA, which has yet to announce the venue for the tournament’s showpiece match.

news.title: UEFA sets new women's football coaching benchmarks and expands pathways for female coaches, women’s football coaches and professional players
news.lede: We're driving a new era of coaching standards in women's club competitions, while expanding access to UEFA Pro Licence courses and creating more flexible pathways for leading coaching talent. As women’s football continues to reach new heights, so must the coaching standards and opportunities that will sustain its success. We are opening more routes to the highest levels of coach education, giving national associations greater flexibility to create places, expand courses and support talented coaches on their journey to UEFA Pro level. From the 2029/30 season, new minimum licence requirements for coaches in UEFA women’s club competitions will also come into force.

news.title: How NFAF Leadership Failures Cost Nigeria Its Flag Football World Championship Spot
news.lede: Nigeria qualified for the 2026 flag football World Championships after winning Africa’s inaugural championships. Then visa delays, funding problems and alleged NFAF failures kept both teams out of Germany.
